title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented on discordant pairs (n = 1, n10 = 1) producing archived two-sided p = 1.00 under the executor’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks such as translation of operator intent to device configuration, multi-step change planning, and programmatic repairs. System reports and surveys emphasize that operational safety depends heavily on surrounding engineering: deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback mechanisms [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A widely proposed operational pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM generates a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks a set of formalized properties, and automated or human-in-the-loop repairs are applied for violations.

Despite conceptual consensus, controlled measurements that isolate the marginal contribution of a verifier (holding the model’s proposal fixed) are scarce. Practitioners must know: when an LLM already produces high-quality candidates, how much incremental safety does a verifier plus a modest automated repair budget provide on a verifier-scoped pass/fail metric? To answer this precisely we preregistered and executed a paired experiment that isolates verifier+repair impact under canonical, deterministic semantics. Our objective was deliberately narrow and operational: given identical initial proposals (shared-initial_candidate semantics), how much does integrating a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM alone?
sections.related_work:
Formal and deterministic verification tools for network configurations and update-safety (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers, Batfish-style analyzers) provide machine-checkable properties such as reachability/isolation and update atomicity; these methods are established in NetOps verification literature and motivate verifier-in-the-loop system designs [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps systems and intent-translation research demonstrate integrations of LLMs for intent parsing and configuration generation while advocating guardrails for operational reliability (e.g., INTA, Confucius, other agentic NetOps frameworks) [INTA, 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair patterns appear across structured-generation domains and have been proposed to reduce incorrect or unsafe outputs [PoeTone; INTA].

Separate literature documents systemic failure modes of LLM-driven automation (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) and recommends verification or human oversight as mitigations [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. What is less prevalent in the supplied evidence is a controlled, preregistered ablation that quantifies the marginal verifier effect while keeping the LLM’s initial output identical for both arms. Our study contributes such an artifact-backed measurement and places it in the context of those prior system reports and verification methods.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026, freezing research questions, inclusion/exclusion rules, task generator seeds, estimands, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule before observing outcomes. Primary confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration and supporting artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest).

Task generation and strata. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was created using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered seeds and deterministic replacement rules. The preregistered stratification allocated tasks across three clusters: VLAN-change (167), ACL-change (167), static-route-change (166). The realized, post-execution per-cluster counts matched the preregistered allocation (VLAN = 167, ACL = 167, static-route = 166); the full task manifest and realized entries are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). To align scope with the verifier, allowed_features were constrained to {admin, mtu, vlan}; tasks referencing features outside the verifier scope were routed to an excluded cohort per the preregistration (no confirmatory exclusions occurred in this run).

Generation semantics and experiment control. To isolate the verifier’s marginal effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false). For each task the pipeline produced a single shared LLM proposal (shared candidate) recorded once; that identical candidate constituted the baseline output and was also validated by the guarded arm. The guarded path executed at most one automated repair call only if the deterministic verifier reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate. This semantics prevents conflation with verifier-guided regeneration and isolates the effect of verification plus at most one repair applied to the same initial proposal.

Models, adapter, and verifier. Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini called through the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses); model parameters and adapter configuration are archived (execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256 recorded in the manifest). The deterministic verifier used for gating and scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; the validator specification and the mapping of violation codes to severity are archived in the evidence bundle. The guarded arm permitted at most one automated repair iteration per preregistered contract.

Statistical plan and implementation. The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. The archived analysis executor implements the exact two-sided McNemar by forming n = n10 + n01 (discordant pairs) and performing an exact binomial test B(n, 0.5) on the observed count n10 (the number of pairs where guarded passes and baseline fails, per the executor’s discordant-ordering convention). We also computed paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs for the absolute difference (B = 10,000, bootstrap_seed = 1729) with task/pair as resampling unit and pairing preserved. All analysis code, seeds, and auxiliary scripts are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact McNemar two-sided p-value and CI. Using the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention yields two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json and the CSVs) and analysis_log.jsonl record these computations and parameters.

Discordant episode provenance and concise artifact-backed summary. The single repair-stage provider call converted one baseline failure into a guarded pass (the lone discordant episode; discordant counts n10 = 1). The full episode record and the verifier/repair traces are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl (archived SHA-256: e7c1fc4d8932389dc3e4c651cf6db08a84ba3a1cd4893b9d7d985618929ff945) and can be deterministically located by filtering that file for entries where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) and guarded scoring indicates pass == 1. To support deterministic audit while avoiding gratuitous operational detail in the publication text, we provide the following concise, artifact-grounded summary extracted verbatim from the archived validator_trace and repair trace for that episode: the verifier reported a preregistered medium-severity sequencing/constraint violation (a required workflow-order constraint for the task payload was not satisfied by the shared candidate), the automated repair iteration injected a single localized sequencing adjustment (reordering a shutdown/field-change pair and emitting the required "admin down" step before the field change per the task policy), and the validator subsequently reported zero high/medium-severity violations on the repaired configuration. The raw per-episode JSON and the repair-provider traces in execution/* contain the complete validator_codes, repair prompt/response, and normalized_configuration for deterministic re-inspection.

Secondary analyses and power divergence. The preregistration assumed a baseline error prevalence around 0.30 for power planning (target absolute reduction 10 percentage points). Observed baseline failure prevalence (1/500) was far lower, producing a ceiling effect and reducing statistical sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements. Consequently, secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative due to near-zero counts. Diagnostics (missingness_summary.csv, contamination_summary.csv, deterministic_reconciliation.json) indicate no exclusions, no contamination flags, and zero failed episodes under the execution contract.

Representative task exemplars. The evidence bundle contains multiple representative task records (execution/responses and execution/scoring JSON artifacts). Example task-000001 in the bundle illustrates a medium-difficulty shutdown→configure→restore pattern where both baseline and guarded produced an identical valid configuration and the verifier reported zero violations. Representative artifacts and their SHA-256 sums are recorded in the manifest to enable deterministic inspection.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained experimental regime — single requested model (gpt-5-mini), deterministic shared-initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair iteration — the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the marginal measured pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This is a conditional result: it documents that when baseline proposal quality is very high on verifier-scoped properties, measurable pass-rate gains from modest verifier+repair budgets may be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric. Importantly, the verifier still exhibited corrective utility by converting one concrete baseline failure into a pass (the single discordant episode archived under execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA above).

Design-choice implications. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate the verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals. This answers the specific operational question of marginal verifier benefit when regeneration costs are constrained or when deployment semantics require a single human-reviewed proposal to be repaired rather than regenerated. The design does not evaluate alternative operational choices such as verifier-guided regeneration, multiple repair iterations, or cost-weighted objective functions; those alternatives may produce different effect sizes and should be measured under their own preregistrations.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic task seeds, and automated replacement rules; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity is limited by the verifier’s modeled property set: pass==no high/medium-severity violations is defined relative to the verifier’s coverage and severity mapping archived in the validator-spec artifacts. If production operators care about properties outside that modeled set (vendor-specific CLI behaviors, dynamic protocol states), the measured pass-rate difference here underestimates the operational benefit of broader verifier coverage. External validity is limited by single-model testing, synthetic task corpus, and constrained feature scope; results are not evidence of multi-model or cross-vendor generality.

Statistical nuance and interpretation. The archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the executor’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs computation and the empirical discordant counts (n = 1). Small-sample exact p-values under such conventions can be non-intuitive; here p = 1.00 indicates the observed discordant pattern (one guarded-only success, zero baseline-only successes) is not unusual under the null when n is so small. The paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.006] provides a complementary uncertainty quantification for the absolute difference. Together these artifacts show that while a point-estimate improvement exists (0.002), inference is constrained by a ceiling effect and by the small number of discordant outcomes.

Operational recommendations. (1) Measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative operational data before allocating expensive repair budgets: when baseline error is extremely low on verifier-scoped properties, marginal pass-rate gains per unit cost may be small. (2) Align verifier property coverage with operator-critical constraints; inspect the archived validator-spec to determine modeled properties and severity mapping and expand verifier coverage where needed. (3) Choose generation semantics to match operational priorities: shared-initial semantics minimize model-call overhead and preserve the original proposal for human review, whereas verifier-guided regeneration may increase final-pass probability at the cost of additional model calls.

Reproducibility and auditability. All artifacts required to reproduce the run are archived in the evidence bundle: preregistration, task generator code and seeds, model_configuration.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA above), execution/task_manifest.jsonl, provider-call traces, validator traces, analysis CSVs, and the deterministic_reconciliation manifest. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 501 and observed repair-stage calls = 1. The exact initial master prompt starting the autonomous research run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and is referenced in the Disclosure Statement. The single discordant episode is locatable deterministically by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces.
sections.conclusion: We performed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), giving an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). This conditional measurement illustrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for the verifier-modeled properties and the verifier’s coverage is limited, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a modest verifier+repair budget can be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric, though the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures. We recommend practitioners measure baseline error prevalence on representative workloads, align verifier coverage with operator-critical properties, and select generation/repair semantics that match deployment priorities. The full preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of every claim made here.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: e7c1fc4d8932389dc3e4c651cf6db08a84ba3a1cd4893b9d7d985618929ff945). To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
